When I was in high school, I had a tendency to be a bit of a procrastinator. This particular summer, my friend Sarah needed help with her essay. She asked me for feedback on her thesis statement. I was eager to assist and agreed to look at it that evening. However, I put it off until the last minute. The next morning, Sarah was expecting me to return the essay with my thoughts. I was rushing to the library, but I had left my notebook at home.

Feeling flustered, I searched for a quick solution. I decided to write a few half-baked ideas in the margins of her essay. I figured it would be enough to make her happy. I handed the paper to Sarah, apologizing for my rushed work. She thanked me and asked me to review it again later. As I walked away
